Area of Habitat (AOH): suitable land cover within a range and elevation band

Source: R/elevation.R
calc_aoh.Rd

Computes the terrestrial Area of Habitat as the suitable land cover within a range polygon, optionally restricted to an elevation band, following the Area-of-Habitat concept (Brooks et al. 2019) and the sRedList workflow (Cazalis et al. 2024). "Suitable" defaults to the natural conservation group of the land-cover legend, so the result is consistent with the natural-versus-converted metrics used elsewhere in mappingAS; supply suitable_groups to change it.

Usage

calc_aoh(
  range,
  year = NULL,
  collection = NULL,
  initiative = "brazil",
  backend = "local",
  src = NULL,
  elev_src = NULL,
  elev_min = NA,
  elev_max = NA,
  z = 9,
  suitable_groups = "natural",
  suitable_codes = NULL,
  marginal_codes = NULL,
  points = NULL,
  max_pixels = 5e+07
)

Arguments

range

An sf/sfc range polygon (e.g. the EOO hull from calc_eoo or the AOO cell union). Points yield NA.

year, collection, initiative, backend, src

Land-cover selection, as in assess_species / mb_raster_local.

elev_src

Optional DEM path/URL used instead of elevatr.

elev_min, elev_max

Elevation band in metres. NA (default) on either side leaves that side open; both NA skips the elevation mask and the AOH is the suitable land cover alone.

z

Terrain-tile zoom for elevatr (default 9). Ignored when elev_src is given.

suitable_groups

Conservation group(s) counted as suitable habitat (default "natural"). See mb_legend.

suitable_codes

Optional integer land-cover class codes counted as suitable, overriding suitable_groups (e.g. the specific classes that make ecological sense for the species).

marginal_codes

Optional integer class codes of marginal or unknown-suitability habitat (sRedList's "Marginal_Unknown"). When supplied, a second, broader AOH (aoh_max_km2) is returned that adds these to the suitable classes, giving a strict-to-broad AOH range.

points

Optional sf of occurrence points; when given, the point_prevalence (share of occurrences inside the suitable habitat) validation metric is returned.

max_pixels

Pixel budget for the land-cover read (default 5e7).

Value

A list with aoh_km2 (suitable area within the elevation band, the AOH), aoh_max_km2 (the broader AOH including marginal classes; equal to aoh_km2 when none), aoo_upper_km2 / aoo_upper_cells (the AOH rescaled to the 2 km reference scale - the IUCN-compliant AOO upper bound - and its cell count), model_prevalence (share of the range that is suitable habitat) and point_prevalence (share of points inside the habitat; NA without points), suitable_km2 (suitable area without the elevation mask, for reference), elev_min, elev_max, elev_applied, suitable_groups, suitable_codes and marginal_codes.

Details

The land cover is read over the range with the same backend as assess_species (MapBiomas or Sentinel-2/Esri) and, when an elevation band is given, an elevation model read over the same extent (windowed; via elev_src or the optional elevatr package) is resampled to the land-cover grid and used to mask out pixels outside [elev_min, elev_max]. The remaining suitable area is the AOH. The read is bounded by max_pixels (the land cover is aggregated with a majority rule beyond that) so a large range does not exhaust memory. This AOH can be passed as the habitat-based upper AOO bound to aoo_bounds.

Every failure (no DEM, no land cover, an unsupported backend) degrades to NA with a message rather than an error.

References

Brooks T.M. et al. (2019) Measuring terrestrial Area of Habitat (AOH) and its utility for the IUCN Red List. Trends in Ecology & Evolution 34:977-986. doi:10.1016/j.tree.2019.06.009

Cazalis V. et al. (2024) Accelerating and standardising IUCN Red List assessments with sRedList. Biological Conservation 298:110761. doi:10.1016/j.biocon.2024.110761

See also

aoo_bounds, elevation_preferences, summarise_conversion

Examples

# \donttest{
f <- system.file("extdata", "example_occurrences.csv", package = "mappingAS")
occ <- read_occurrences(f)
sp1 <- occ[occ$species == occ$species[1], ]
hull <- calc_eoo(sp1)$hull
# Reads MapBiomas land cover (and a DEM if elevatr is installed):
calc_aoh(hull, year = 2024, elev_min = 0, elev_max = 1500)
#> $aoh_km2
#> [1] 1370.189
#> 
#> $aoh_max_km2
#> [1] 1370.189
#> 
#> $suitable_km2
#> [1] 1370.189
#> 
#> $aoo_upper_km2
#> [1] 2708
#> 
#> $aoo_upper_cells
#> [1] 677
#> 
#> $model_prevalence
#> [1] 0.5551775
#> 
#> $point_prevalence
#> [1] NA
#> 
#> $elev_min
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $elev_max
#> [1] 1500
#>

#>
